item.title: CAFR: Context-Aware Feature Refinement for Narrow Field-of-View Cross-View Geo-Localization
item.description: While existing work in cross-view geo-localization (CVGL) predominantly localizes 360° panoramic images using satellite imagery, real-world query images often have a narrow field-of-view (NFoV). This narrower field-of-view (FoV) results in a significantly smaller overlapping region between the query and the satellite image, posing a distinct challenge. In narrow CVGL (NCVGL), existing methods lack effective supervision mechanisms to guide models toward overlapping regions, rendering them vulnerable to nonoverlapping content. To address this, we propose context-aware feature refinement (CAFR). Its core innovation lies in a novel feature learning approach: it converts geometric priors within overlapping regions into differentiable supervision signals that directly constrain the cross-attention matrices of features, thereby steering representation learning. CAFR incorporates two key modules: 1) salient region separation (SRS), enforcing spatial consistency between the attention matrices and overlapping regions through a novel saliency separation loss and 2) coordinate-weighted regression (CWR), aligning attention peaks with region centers via a regression loss to enhance feature discriminability. To evaluate model performance under more realistic conditions, we collected user-uploaded real-world images to construct the cross-view narrow FoV (CVNAF) dataset. It is the first NCVGL benchmark that contains perspective images and establishes projection relationships between ground and satellite imagery, offering a realistic evaluation setting for follow-up research. Extensive experiments show that CAFR achieves state-of-the-art (SOTA) performance, improving R@1 by over 5% on multiple NCVGL benchmarks. The code and dataset are released at https://github.com/Hobe-Frank/CAFR
item.authors: Mingbo Hou;Xiaofei Hu;Yang Zhou;Luying Zhao;Mengyuan Zhu;

item.title: Peak Energy Synchroextracting Transform and Its Application in Reservoir Reflection Interface Identification
item.description: Time–frequency analysis methods serve as vital tools in seismic data processing, enabling the extraction of key geological information from seismic reflection data. While postprocessing techniques based on instantaneous frequency (IF) and group delay estimation are widely applied in fields such as sedimentary cycle division and the identification of tight sandstone gas reservoirs, they still exhibit limitations in identifying reflection interfaces. To address this gap, this study focuses on deriving reflection interface information from seismic reflection data and proposes a novel method termed the peak energy synchroextracting transform (PESET). First, based on the seismic bandwidth signal and its time–frequency energy distribution characteristics, this method achieves precise mapping by correlating the peak energy of the stacked short-time Fourier transform (STFT) time–frequency spectrum along the time axis with the temporal positions of reflection interfaces. Then, we theoretically derive the range of the parameter necessary to preserve this correspondence. Finally, the time–frequency coefficients at the corresponding moments are extracted as the final representation. Theoretical tests and applications to field seismic data demonstrate that the proposed PESET method accurately identifies and precisely locates reservoir reflection interfaces.

item.title: Toward Realistic Remote Sensing Dataset Distillation With Discriminative Prototype-Guided Diffusion
item.description: Recent years have witnessed the remarkable success of deep learning in remote sensing image interpretation, driven by the availability of large-scale benchmark datasets. However, this reliance on massive training data also brings substantial storage and computational costs. To address this challenge, this study introduces the concept of dataset distillation into the field of remote sensing image interpretation for the first time. Specifically, we propose discriminative prototype-guided diffusion (DPD), a diffusion-based generative distillation framework that condenses a large-scale remote sensing dataset into a compact and representative distilled dataset. To improve the semantic fidelity and diversity of the synthesized samples, we extract representative prototypes for each category in the latent space. We then construct hyperspherical semantic anchors around the prototypes to guide the reverse denoising trajectory. Furthermore, to enhance the discriminative quality of the generated samples, multiple candidates are generated for each prototype and ranked by a latent classifier using a logit-margin criterion, with the most discriminative candidates selected to form the final distilled dataset. Experiments on three high-resolution remote sensing scene classification benchmarks show that the proposed method can distill realistic, diverse, and discriminative samples for downstream model training. Code and pretrained models are available online (https://github.com/YonghaoXu/DPD).

item.title: Beyond Specific Degradations: Prompt-Driven Spatial–Spectral Modeling for Hyperspectral Image Enhancement
item.description: Hyperspectral images (HSIs) are often degraded by complex and coupled corruptions such as noise, blur, and haze. Most existing methods are designed for specific degradation types, lacking the flexibility for unified enhancement. In addition, jointly modeling spatial structures and spectral correlations remains challenging. In this article, we propose a prompt-driven spatial–spectral framework for HSI enhancement, which improves adaptability across diverse degradations via semantic–visual–spectral (SVS) multiprompt learning. The proposed framework introduces cross-modal prompts to provide adaptive guidance, enabling the model to handle diverse, mixed, and shifted degradation patterns within the considered HSI degradation space. To extract richer spatial representations, we design a direction-aware rectangle self-attention (DRSA) mechanism. It effectively captures horizontal and vertical dependencies to better restore anisotropic structures while reducing computational cost compared with dense global self-attention. To preserve spectral fidelity, we introduce a frequency-aware prompt-guided spectral modulation (FPSM) mechanism, which dynamically modulates spectral features using a learnable spectral prototype bank. We further devise a cross-modal semantic–visual dynamic prompting (SVDP) mechanism that integrates textual degradation descriptions and visual prototypes to generate degradation-aware prompts, enabling adaptive perception of diverse corruption patterns. Extensive experiments on remote sensing HSI datasets show that the proposed method achieves performance superior to state-of-the-art methods. It consistently improves both visual quality and spectral accuracy under various degradation conditions. These results validate the potential of multiprompt learning for unified HSI enhancement tasks.
item.authors: Huan Wang;Jing Gao;Pengju Si;Yiwei Li;Lifan Sun;Jun Wang;Fazhan Tao;Fengxun Zheng;Baofeng Ji;

item.title: Inside the Area of Applicability: Feature-Space Reliability Diagnostics Can Miss Failures in a Grassland Biomass Map
item.description: The area of applicability (AOA) marks where a machine learning map is expected, on average, to reach its cross-validated accuracy, by flagging locations whose predictors are unlike the training data. This assumes that predictor unfamiliarity helps identify where predictions fail. We tested that assumption on a grassland aboveground biomass (AGB) map of Inner Mongolia, from 418 field plots and a multisource random forest (RF). The AOA admitted 91.4% of plots. Shrub desert was the worst-predicted vegetation type, and about 90% of its plots remained inside the AOA under all nine implementations tested. Within the AOA, 52 plots on cover types outside the grassland target had an RMSE of 109.3 g m−2, 1.95 times the pooled cross-validation RMSE of 56.0 g m−2, compared with 38.8 g m−2 for 310 grassland plots with statistically indistinguishable measured biomass. For shrub desert, prediction–observation correlation was 0.15, compared with 0.78 for grassland, with no detectable bias. Only a rule derived from an external vegetation map separated relative-error distributions (p $= 5\times 10^{-4}$ ); predictor-space distance, the dissimilarity index (DI), and ensemble disagreement did not. A controlled mixture built from the same predictors illustrates how this pattern can arise. When two response regimes shared the same predictor distribution, the tested diagnostics showed little separation, and the ratio of the failing regime’s RMSE to pooled cross-validation RMSE rose from 1.17 at half the extent to 1.91 at 5%. Regional maps spanning more than one response regime should therefore report the composition of their extent alongside their headline accuracy.
item.authors: Xinyu Chen;Xiaohua Zhu;Guangzhou Ouyang;Lingling Ma;Wei Liu;Xinfang Yuan;Qi Wang;

item.title: SCD-MoE: Adaptive Expert Routing for Efficient Remote Sensing Semantic Change Detection
item.description: Semantic change detection (SCD) aims to simultaneously localize changed regions and identify land-cover transitions from bi-temporal images. However, existing methods usually process bi-temporal features with fixed interaction structures or shared fusion functions, providing limited flexibility to explicitly adapt interaction preferences to diverse change patterns. In addition, SCD requires both change localization and semantic recognition, which emphasize different information cues: the former relies more on discrepancy-sensitive features, while the latter requires semantic-preserving and region-consistent representations, yet such task-specific preferences are often insufficiently modeled. To address these challenges, we propose SCD-mixture-of-expert (MoE), an efficient dynamic framework that leverages conditional computation to model sample-adaptive interactions and task-specific feature preferences. First, we introduce an interaction-adaptive MoE (IA-MoE), which routes bi-temporal features to difference-aware and semantic-preserving experts for adaptive interaction modeling. Through selective expert weighting, IA-MoE enhances change-related cues while maintaining semantic context. Second, we develop a task-aware routing MoE (TAR-MoE), which employs task-specific gates over a shared expert pool to generate localization- and recognition-oriented representations. This design enables controlled information sharing while allowing each task to emphasize suitable feature transformations. Experiments on three benchmarks show that SCD-MoE consistently achieves superior performance, including a 5.04% separated Kappa coefficient (SeK) improvement on Landsat-SCD, while using only 48% of the parameters and substantially fewer FLOPs compared with the previous state-of-the-art method. Code and pretrained models will be made available at https://github.com/HuQ1an/SCD-MoE
item.authors: Qian Hu;Haoran Zhu;Yan Zhang;Fang Xu;Haijian Zhang;Wen Yang;

item.title: 3-D MCSEM Forward Modeling With Mixed-Order Spectral-Element Method Based on Nonconformal Meshes
item.description: In 3-D forward modeling of marine controlled-source electromagnetic (MCSEM) methods, to accurately resolve the fine-scale reservoirs, a fine discretization in the vicinity of target bodies is generally required. However, when using high-accuracy modeling methods like the spectral-element (SE) methods, the degrees of freedom (DoF) and the size of the coefficient matrix grow rapidly with the order of interpolation bases, leading to higher computational costs and limiting their application in large-scale, high-resolution MCSEM modeling. To solve this problem, we develop a mixed-order spectral-element (mSE) method based on nonconformal meshes for efficient 3-D MCSEM modeling. In this method, the local areas that contain reservoirs are defined as target subdomains, while the remaining area is treated as the background. The mesh resolution and the order of interpolation basis functions in each subdomain can be independently set, resulting in nonconformity at the domain interfaces. To ensure stable transmission of electromagnetic (EM) energy across these nonconformal interfaces, we impose Robin-type transmission conditions based on the continuity of the vector and scalar potentials. Subsequently, the local equations for each subdomain are built separately and then assembled via local–global mapping, ultimately forming a global system of equations for calculating 3-D EM responses. Numerical experiments for typical models and a realistic 3-D hydrocarbon reservoir structure demonstrate that our method can significantly reduce the computational time and memory usage while maintaining high accuracy, providing an efficient tool for large-scale 3-D MCSEM forward modeling.
item.authors: Shuai Yan;Changchun Yin;Jiao Zhu;Bo Zhang;Xiuyan Ren;Yang Su;Yunhe Liu;Jun Li;Luyuan Wang;Mingquan Lai;Yue Yang;

item.title: UHR-DETR: Efficient End-to-End Small Object Detection for Ultrahigh-Resolution Remote Sensing Imagery
item.description: The ultrahigh-resolution (UHR) imagery has become essential for modern remote sensing, offering unprecedented spatial coverage. However, detecting small objects in such vast scenes presents a critical dilemma: retaining the original resolution for small objects causes prohibitive memory bottlenecks. Conversely, the conventional compromises, such as image downsampling or patch cropping, either erase small objects or destroy context. To break this dilemma, we propose UHR-DETR, an efficient end-to-end transformer-based detector designed for UHR imagery. First, we introduce a coverage-maximizing sparse encoder that dynamically allocates finite computational resources to informative high-resolution regions, ensuring maximum object coverage with minimal spatial redundancy. Second, we design a global–local decoupled decoder. By integrating macroscopic scene awareness with microscopic object details, this module resolves semantic ambiguities and prevents scene fragmentation. Extensive experiments on the UHR imagery datasets (e.g., STAR and SODA-A) demonstrate the superiority of UHR-DETR under strict hardware constraints (e.g., a single 24GB RTX 3090). It achieves a 2.8% mean average precision (mAP) improvement while delivering a $9\times $ inference speedup compared to standard sliding-window baselines on the STAR dataset. Our code and models are available at https://github.com/Li-JingFang/UHR-DETR
item.authors: Jingfang Li;Haoran Zhu;Wen Yang;Jinrui Zhang;Fang Xu;Haijian Zhang;Gui-Song Xia;

item.title: A Unified Novel Architectural Paradigm for Remote Sensing Change Detection
item.description: In recent years, remote sensing change detection (CD) has garnered significant attention due to its critical role in resource monitoring and disaster assessment. CD tasks exist with different output granularities such as binary CD (BCD), semantic CD (SCD), and building damage assessment (BDA). However, existing methods require substantial expert knowledge to design specialized decoders that compensate for information loss during encoding across different tasks. This not only introduces uncertainty into the process of selecting optimal models for abrupt change scenarios (such as disaster outbreaks) but also limits the universality of these architectures. To address these challenges, a unified, general CD framework named unified novel architectural paradigm for remote sensing CD (UniRSCD) is proposed here. Building upon a state space model (SSM) backbone, a frequency change prompt generator (FCPG) as a unified encoder is introduced. The encoder dynamically scans bitemporal global context information while integrating high-frequency details with low-frequency holistic information, thereby eliminating the need for specialized decoders for feature compensation. Subsequently, the unified decoder and prediction head establish a shared representation space through hierarchical feature interaction and task-adaptive output mapping. This integrates various tasks such as BCD and SCD into a unified architecture, thereby accommodating the differing output granularity requirements of distinct CD tasks. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed architecture can adapt to multiple CD tasks and achieves leading performance on five datasets, including the binary change dataset LEVIR-CD, the semantic change dataset SECOND, and the BDA dataset xBD. The source code is available at: https://github.com/zhenliuzhenqi
item.authors: Yuan Qu;Zhipeng Zhang;Chaojun Xu;Qiao Wan;Yuzeng Chen;Zhenqi Liu;Yanfei Zhong;Jón Atli Benediktsson;

item.title: A Low-Complexity Separated Space–Time IAA-LS Method With Local Joint Refinement for Forward-Looking Super-Resolution Imaging
item.description: Forward-looking array radar imaging is limited by weak Doppler discrimination in the forward-looking region, which leads to poor angular resolution and makes closely spaced mainlobe targets difficult to resolve. A full-dimensional space–time iterative adaptive approach with least-squares implementation (ST-IAA-LS) can provide high angular resolution by jointly exploiting spatial and slow-time degrees of freedom, but its practical use is hindered by the high computational cost caused by the construction and inversion of a large space–time covariance matrix. This article proposes a low-complexity separated space–time IAA-LS method for forward-looking super-resolution imaging. Instead of directly constructing the full $N_{s}N_{t}$ -dimensional covariance matrix, the proposed method alternately performs temporal IAA-LS focusing and spatial IAA-LS refinement, thereby reducing the dominant inversion cost to two low-dimensional covariance updates. To avoid the performance loss caused by a simple independent separation, an angle-Doppler coupling power update is introduced to preserve the association between temporal Doppler responses and spatial angular responses. Matched-filter initialization, adaptive diagonal loading, damped power updates, and power-floor protection are further incorporated to improve numerical stability under finite snapshots and noise. In addition, a focused local joint refinement stage is designed for selected candidate angles to recover part of the full space–time processing gain while avoiding full-dimensional covariance inversion. Simulations and measured data results show that the proposed method achieves an angular resolution that is only slightly degraded compared to full-dimensional ST-IAA-LS, yet its computational cost is significantly reduced.
item.authors: Lingyun Ren;Di Wu;Zhenyuan Li;Guodong Jin;Daiyin Zhu;

item.title: RainDSD: Joint Retrieval of Rain Rate and Drop-Size Distribution Parameters From GPM Microwave Imager
item.description: The passive-microwave (PMW) radiometers, such as the global precipitation measurement (GPM) microwave imager (GMI), observe precipitation across 13 channels from 10 to 183 GHz, where brightness temperatures respond to hydrometeor emission and scattering and therefore contain information about precipitation microphysics. However, most PMW algorithms reduce this multichannel signal to a single bulk rain rate (RR), leaving the drop size distribution (DSD) largely accessible only through active radar. In this study, we present RainDSD, a multitask convolutional encoder–decoder that jointly retrieves RR and the two governing DSD parameters, mass-weighted mean diameter ${D}_{m}$ and normalized intercept ${N}_{w}$ , directly from GMI radiances, using collocated dual-frequency precipitation radar (DPR) retrievals as a reference. Because RR is an integral over the same drop spectrum parameterized by ${D}_{m}$ and ${N}_{w}$ , a shared encoder exploits their physical coupling, while featurewise linear modulation (FiLM) on surface type supports retrieval over land and coast. On an independent full-year 2022 test set and an identical-pixel mask, RainDSD improves RR retrieval over the Goddard Profiling Algorithm (GPROF) version 7 (GPROF V07), with $r^{2}$ increasing from 0.503 to 0.762 and root-mean-square error (RMSE) decreasing from 2.23 to 1.55 mm/h; the largest gains occur over land, coast, and in heavy rain. In addition, RainDSD retrieves ${D}_{m}$ ( ${r}^{2} =0.623$ ) and ${N}_{w}$ ( ${r}^{2} =0.479$ ), evaluated as compared to DPR, from PMW observation alone. This represents the first PMW retrieval of these DSD parameters, enabling their placement within established precipitation regime space and revealing coherent latitudinal structures, including signatures associated with the intertropical convergence zone (ITCZ). These results demonstrate that multichannel PMW observations carry recoverable information about precipitation microphysical structure across the radiometer swath.

item.title: Spectral Gradient Field-Guided Bayesian Adaptive Graph Convolution for Hyperspectral Image Classification
item.description: Graph-based deep learning methods play a significant role in hyperspectral image classification (HSIC). Nonetheless, the paucity of prior information to construct graph model structures continues to severely challenge the classification of images characterized by significant spatial heterogeneity. To achieve effective adaptive construction of graph model structures, this article proposes a spectral-driven self-adapting graph construction framework. A spectral gradient field (SGF) is introduced to quantify the local rate and direction of spectral variation, enabling dynamic adjustment of node connections according to spatial–spectral characteristics. The method adaptively expands or contracts neighborhood scopes based on local spectral gradients, effectively addressing over- and under-segmentation problems in complex regions. Furthermore, a beta distribution is employed to model the probabilistic connectivity between nodes, enhancing the robustness of graph topology. For large hyperspectral scenes, constructing and storing a full graph leads to prohibitive memory consumption and computational cost. To address this issue, we extend the proposed method to a block-wise and pruned Bayesian adaptive graph convolutional network (BP-BAGCN), in which images are divided into nonoverlapping or lightly overlapping spatial blocks; then the local maps are constructed, refined, and inferred independently. Experiments are conducted on three hyperspectral datasets: a benchmark dataset and two newly constructed datasets derived from GF-5 satellite observations over complex coastal wetlands, providing challenging real-world scenarios with rich spectral variability and ecological diversity. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method consistently outperforms state-of-the-art approaches under limited labeled samples. Across five independent random seeds, the proposed method achieves average overall accuracies of 98.79% $\pm ~0.70$ %, 99.35% $\pm ~0.13$ %, and 92.27% $\pm ~0.65$ % on the three datasets, respectively, demonstrating both superior classification performance and stable generalization ability.

item.title: Hierarchical Progressive Distillation for Image Super-Resolution of Remote Sensing
item.description: Remote sensing image super-resolution (SR) fundamentally relies on effective feature representation learning. However, the existing methods that adopt mainstream architecture designs, such as transformer and state space model (SSM), are often restricted by two factors when dealing with the SR of remote sensing images. Initially, to overcome the limitations of shallow networks and achieve sufficient depth in feature extraction, constructing deeper network architectures is inevitable, which increases the model’s parametric complexity and computational cost. On the other hand, as network depth increases continuously, the transmission efficiency of information flow across different hierarchical levels declines markedly. Key features undergo gradual attenuation during successive transformation processes, giving rise to the loss of critical information. We propose a novel hierarchical progressive distillation (HPD) framework to alleviate this predicament, which establishes a systematic hierarchical path for feature refinement. While eliminating redundant computations, it can better preserve semantic information. Subsequently, given the potential for global information loss during distillation, we propose spatial-frequency hybrid attention (SHA) to enhance feature representation. In particular, SHA adaptively captures spatial dependencies of different scales by integrating dynamic window attention (DWA) and multiscale frequency attention (MFA), and optimizes frequency processing to provide global context modeling. A large number of experiments we conducted across multiple public remote sensing datasets show that our method achieves a trade-off among model parameters, computational overhead, and performance, and outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods.
item.authors: Kanghui Zhao;Tao Lu;Jiaming Wang;Yanduo Zhang;Junjun Jiang;Zhongyuan Wang;

item.title: SAM-STF: A Multibranch SAM-Guided Spatial–Temporal-Frequency Aware Framework for Semantic Change Detection
item.description: Semantic change detection (SCD) aims to determine whether land-cover categories change and how they evolve across multitemporal remote sensing images. Despite recent advances, existing methods still face some challenges. First, the encoders of visual foundation models produce overly smoothed representations, weakening fine-grained boundary information that is essential for object-level changes. Second, common temporal modeling strategies, such as feature differencing or fusion, fail to capture bitemporal interactions and recognize subtle changes. Third, relying on a single backbone often fails to achieve a tradeoff between global semantic consistency and local spatial precision. As such, we propose a novel multibranch segment anything model (SAM)-guided spatial–temporal-frequency aware framework (SAM-STF) for SCD. It adopts a two-stream Siamese encoder, where the frozen SAM branch is introduced to capture global semantic context and boundary priors, while the lightweight ResNet34 branch delivers fine-grained local spatial details. In particular, we design a sample-specific low-rank modulation (S2LoRM) module to provide input-conditioned low-rank residual modulation for the SAM branch. To enhance the boundary clarity of the changed areas, we design an adaptive Gaussian-derivative projection (AGDP) module that refines shallow SAM features through multidirectional Gaussian derivative filtering. In addition, a bidirectional temporal-frequency awareness (BTFA) module is developed to symmetrically model bidirectional temporal interactions while integrating multiscale spatial context and frequency-domain information. Therefore, subtle and complex bitemporal changes can be located and detected, offering more precise boundary description and stronger robustness to complex spatial–temporal scenarios. Extensive experiments on three benchmark datasets demonstrate that SAM-STF achieves the best performance, with a separated kappa (SeK) of 65.92% on the Landsat-SCD dataset, 24.67% on the SECOND dataset, and 48.02% on the JL1H dataset, respectively. The code will be available at https://github.com/SUPERMAN123000/SAM-STF
item.authors: Yun-Cheng Li;Heng-Chao Li;Wen-Shuai Hu;Sen Lei;Qian Du;

item.title: SlotATR: Toward Object-Centric Learning for SAR Target Recognition
item.description: Synthetic aperture radar (SAR) images are inherently affected by complex and heterogeneous clutter, whose scattering characteristics often overlap with those of targets and vary across sensing conditions. This leads to severe feature entanglement and degraded generalization in automatic target recognition (ATR), particularly under varying clutter distributions and signal-to-clutter ratio (SCR). To address this challenge, we propose SlotATR, an object-centric learning (OCL)-based ATR framework that disentangles target representations from background clutter in SAR images without requiring mask annotations, and performs ATR using the isolated target features. SlotATR consists of two stages. In the first stage, SlotSAR introduces a grouping feature refinement module (GFRM), which integrates semantic and scattering features to refine the feature space referenced during slot updates. This design facilitates more reliable slot competition, leading to improved object-centric representations. In the second stage, SlotCLS utilizes the disentangled target slot representations to produce target-centric features for ATR classification under cluttered conditions. Extensive experiments on ATRNet-STAR under diverse clutter conditions demonstrate that the proposed framework consistently improves both object-centric decomposition and ATR performance, particularly under challenging clutter variations. These results indicate that SlotATR enhances target–clutter separability in SAR imagery, providing a practical approach toward object-centric SAR image analysis in remote sensing.

item.title: FlexSnow: A Flexible Snow Optics Model Framework Integrating Diverse Snow Microstructures and Light-Absorbing Constituent Mixtures in Multiple Layers
item.description: Optical scattering of snow is complicated by the diversity in the microstructure and composition of snow grains. A flexible snow optics model framework (FlexSnow) is developed to quantify the effects of ice grains’ shape and size, and of the mixing with light-absorbing constituents (LACs) on the surface albedo and bidirectional reflectance of multilayer snowpack. Single-scattering properties (SSPs), particularly including single-scattering albedo, phase function, and mass extinction cross section, are employed for ice grains in the shapes of sphere, ellipsoid, hexagonal plate, Koch snowflake, and as the random bicontinuous medium in various specific surface area (SSA) equivalent radii, and for LACs including various types of soot, dust, and snow algae, as well as liquid water as the spherical shape. The SSPs of ice grains are calculated with a ray-tracing code and the bicontinuous snow model, while the SSPs of light-absorbing impurities are derived from the optical library of the snow, ice, and aerosol radiative (SNICAR) model. The external mixture of ice and LACs allows for the ensemble-averaging of SSPs. The parameterized internal mixing schemes of ice with black carbon and with dust are used to characterize the enhanced coalbedo of snow. Wet snow grains are also approximated by the water-coated ice spheres, and associated SSPs are resolved with Mie calculations. Sensitivity analysis indicates that the effects of various snow grain shapes can be mitigated with the SSA-equivalent radius specification. The distinct absorption features of soot, dust, snow algae, and liquid water in snow, along with the effects of their mixing state, are clearly resolved by FlexSnow. The FlexSnow model compares well against the close-range measurements of pure snow, polluted snow, algal snow, and wet snow, and against the at-sensor observation of fresh snow. Optimal matching of albedo and reflectance measurements demands delicate specification of snow microstructure and LACs mixing, along with subtle tuning of vertical profiles. The FlexSnow modeling framework integrates a variety of advanced characterization strategies for snow SSPs and is expected to facilitate the forward modeling of snow optical remote sensing.
item.authors: Gongxue Wang;Tiancheng Lei;Lingmei Jiang;Jiancheng Shi;Donghui Xie;Fangbo Pan;Yiting Wang;Shuhua Zhang;

item.title: A Depth-Aware Ensemble Deep Learning Framework With Layer-Wise Recursive Prediction for Multisource Subsurface Ocean Temperature and Salinity Forecasting
item.description: Accurate prediction of upper ocean temperature (UOT) and salinity (SS) within the critical 0–50-m depth range is essential for understanding climate variability and supporting sustainable marine ecosystem management. However, existing approaches often struggle to capture complex spatiotemporal dependencies and explicitly model vertical interactions across ocean depths, particularly when integrating heterogeneous data sources. This study proposes a depth-resolved upper ocean forecasting framework with three main contributions. First, a structured multisource data fusion strategy integrates satellite remote sensing products with in situ Argo float observations to enhance the spatial and vertical representation of upper ocean conditions. Second, an ensemble multimodel (EMM) architecture combines complementary deep learning models, including a transformer-based spatiotemporal transformer (TST) model, a standard transformer, long short-term memory (LSTM), and gated recurrent unit (GRU) networks, to learn oceanographic dynamics from heterogeneous observations. Third, a layer-wise depth recursive prediction (LDRP) strategy conditions deeper layer predictions on predicted states from shallower layers, enabling explicit modeling of vertical dependencies without relying on deeper layer ground truth during inference. Experiments conducted on a multisource Western Pacific dataset demonstrate consistent improvements in depth-resolved forecasting accuracy across multiple subsurface layers compared with standalone baseline models, with stronger gains observed for temperature forecasting and task-dependent improvements for SS forecasting. The proposed method provides a robust and depth-resolved forecasting framework for upper ocean monitoring, climate analysis, and marine resource management.
item.authors: Yue-Shan Chang;Yan-Jhen Liao;Basanta Haobijam;Tourangbam Harishore Singh;

item.title: Physics-Data-Coupled Network for Typhoon Satellite Cloud Image Sequence Prediction
item.description: Accurate prediction of typhoon satellite cloud image sequences is essential for short-term typhoon monitoring and forecasting, including center localization, intensity estimation, and evolution analysis. Although deep learning methods have been widely used for typhoon satellite cloud image sequence prediction, they often fail to preserve key cloud structures and maintain motion-coherent evolution. To address these issues, we propose a physics-data-coupled network, termed PhyDC-Net, for typhoon satellite cloud image sequence prediction, in which an architectural design inspired by the transport–source structure of the atmospheric continuity equation is introduced to structure latent-state evolution. The proposed framework consists of two key modules. We design a physics-inspired gated recurrent unit (Phy-GRU) for the recurrent prediction layer. Inspired by the atmospheric continuity equation, this unit decouples the evolution process into a trend-dominated advection term and a transient-variation-driven residual correction term. This design introduces a physics-inspired inductive bias into recurrent prediction. To better capture the complex spatiotemporal evolution of typhoons, we further design a spatial-frequency spatiotemporal LSTM (SFT-LSTM) unit. SFT-LSTM replaces the conventional convolutional feature extractor in ST-LSTM with an integrated dual-branch feature extraction module whose outputs are used for subsequent gated updates. By combining hierarchical residual connections with the discrete cosine transform (DCT), SFT-LSTM jointly models spatial- and frequency-domain features, which improves the representation of fine cloud structures and rapidly varying patterns. Quantitative and qualitative experiments on the Digital Typhoon dataset show that PhyDC-Net outperforms representative baseline methods across multiple evaluation metrics, achieving an SSIM of 0.8138 and reducing mse by 17.2%. The results indicate that PhyDC-Net captures the large-scale motion of typhoon cloud systems while better preserving fine-grained structures, such as the typhoon eye, leading to more accurate and stable predictions.
item.authors: Liling Zhao;Xinyue Wang;Runling Yu;Min Xia;Jiawei Yuan;Fancheng Meng;

item.title: WamBANet: A Wavelet-Guided State-Space Modeling and Semantic Regularization for Weakly Supervised Salient Object Detection in Optical Remote Sensing Images
item.description: Salient object detection (SOD) in optical remote sensing images (ORSIs) remains fundamentally challenging due to extreme object-scale variations, complex background textures, and ambiguous foreground–background separations. While scribble-based weak supervision significantly reduces annotation costs, the inherent sparsity of scribble labels introduces significant structural uncertainty during dense prediction, frequently resulting in boundary erosion and interior collapse. Existing approaches alleviate this issue by incorporating external edge-detection networks or boundary pseudo-labels, but such strategies incur additional computational overhead and often introduce noisy background edges that degrade detection accuracy. To address these limitations, we present WamBANet, a wavelet-guided state-space modeling framework for scribble-supervised ORSI-SOD that enhances structural boundary cues without external edge detectors or boundary pseudo-labels. The proposed wavelet state-space model boundary attention (WamBA) module couples wavelet-derived high-frequency structural priors with SS2D-based low-frequency contextual modeling, enabling complementary semantic–structural refinement under sparse supervision. In addition, the semantic-guided attention enhancement (SGAE) module injects high-level semantic priors into low-level representations to reinforce interior–boundary consistency and suppress hollow-region artifacts. Extensive experiments on the ORSSD and EORSSD datasets demonstrate that WamBANet consistently outperforms state-of-the-art (SOTA) weakly supervised methods and achieves performance comparable to fully supervised models. Cross-dataset evaluations and camouflage object detection experiments further demonstrate the generalization and extensibility of the proposed WamBANet model. Code and experimental results will be made publicly accessible at https://github.com/HAID-LAB/WamBANet
item.authors: Tae Hun Lee;Seunghyeon Yu;Jae Yeol Lee;
